celebrity

/suh-LEB-rih-tee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Celebrity means a widely known, famous person, especially in entertainment or public life.

The retired astronaut discovered that being a celebrity meant never finishing a meal in an airport without signing something.

Worked Example

When twelve-year-old Marcus won the national spelling bee on live television, his life changed for exactly one month. Morning shows flew him to New York, a cereal company mailed him a year of free breakfast, and strangers in three states asked to film him spelling their names. "Our little celebrity," his aunt teased — and for that month, with cameras following a kid everyone suddenly recognized, she wasn't wrong.

Being recognized and sought out by strangers and television shows — fame attached to a person — is what makes Marcus, briefly, a celebrity.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

star: A star is a famous performer or athlete celebrated for talent -- the word points at excellence in entertainment or sports. A celebrity is anyone widely known, deserving or not: fame can attach to a person the cameras follow for no achievement at all. Every star is a celebrity, but plenty of celebrities have no craft behind the fame.

icon: An icon is a famous figure who has come, usually over many years, to stand for something larger -- an era, a style, a movement. A celebrity is simply a person the wide public knows right now. Icon status must be earned by time and meaning; celebrity can arrive in a single viral month.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

nobody: a person of no fame or influence

unknown: a person the public has never heard of

Where it sits · how widely the fame reaches — notable → celebrity → superstar

notable vs. celebrity: A notable is known within a field or a town; a celebrity is recognized by the general public far beyond it.

superstar vs. celebrity: A superstar out-shines an ordinary celebrity — fame so large that a single name fills stadiums.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — celebr

Root — celebr: thronged, much-visited, famous (Latin celeber)

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: the state or condition of

Put it together

Put it together: Celebrity descends from Latin celeber, 'thronged, much-visited' — in Rome, a celebrated place was literally one crowds flocked to. The suffix -ity names a condition, so celebrity is 'the condition of being thronged.' English then did something curious: it turned the condition into the person, so today the celebrity is the one the crowd is pressing around.

Use the root in a new word: celebrated

Use the root in a new word: celebrated: A celebrated author is one the public has gathered around in admiration — the same Latin root celeber, 'thronged, famous,' that turns a person into a celebrity.
